content:
Marro doesn't touch the satchel yet. He leans in, chin on his knuckles, and the candlelight catches the scars that thread his left cheek. "Seal's whole," he says, reading the wax the way other men read faces. "Harbormaster's office, then. Good." He finally sets a palm flat on the leather and waits, the way a man waits for a bomb to decide whether to go off. Outside, rain still hisses against the window. Somewhere down the harbor, a foghorn moans — long and low, swallowed by the downpour. "Forty, like we agreed," he repeats, slower now, testing the words. His eyes flick once past your shoulder to the door, then back to you. "You're a courier who names his price twice. What else did you forget to tell me?" :::card title="The satchel's seal"
⚓
WAX SEAL — INTACT
OriginHarbormaster's Office
Destination— unmarked —
Weightlight; paper
Fee40 gold
:::

Marro's eyes track the satchel before it touches the wood. He unseals it, checks the contents by the guttering lantern—some folded charts, salt-stained and damp at the edges—and nods once, like a man confirming a shipment he's never actually seen.

"Forty, like we agreed," he murmurs, and slides a pouch of heavy coins across the table, his ink-stained thumb brushing a smudge off the leather. The coins ring sharp and clean in the dim. "Word is the Admiralty's charts came loose off a wreck. Don't go making it your habit to handle Admiralty paper, Rook." He leans in, lowering his voice under the bar's noise. "But since you're holding it — the captain you delivered for? He's a dead man's shadow now. The watch has started asking questions at the docks."

Outside, a bell chimes somewhere down the alley — the harbor watch changing shift. Marro's jaw tightens. "So. If you're taking the gold, you might as well take the next piece of work while you're sitting. I need a letter into the Cathedral Ward before dawn. Past two watch checkpoints that've never liked the look of me."

The cudgel cracks across your ribs and the alley walls ring with it. You gasp — the blow has cost you breath — and bring your shortsword up as Gessa follows with a two-handed overhead swing.

She's big, slow to pivot, and her one good eye is fixed on your chest, not your blade. Your ribs scream with every breath you push out, but there's an opening where her guard hangs low on her left side.

The harbormaster's hand closes over the ledger like a man catching rain in a cupped palm. His eyes flick to the bruise blooming along your ribs. 'Midnight. Good.' He presses a small purse into your fist — fifteen gold on top of the favor — and his voice drops. 'The man who hired Gessa has not come forward. That worries me more than the ledger did.'

The bells' last note dies. Rain ticks against the tower glass.

Marro's eyes flick to the satchel, then back to you. "Last seen in the Saltmaster's office — top drawer, under a false bottom. Word is a dockside rat got it in a swap of a stolen cutlass." He taps the table. "By dawn, Rook. The harbormaster's got eyes on that office already."
